| [CLAIM-578](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-578.md) v2 | Computational complexity belongs to a family of problems posed over configuration spaces, with an encoding and permitted operations, and not to a configuration space: one fixed finite space has none, and over the same instances finding a solution and navigating between solutions can fall in different classes | A's proposal, from the pasted synthesis on resource-bounded realizability (three responses, pasted by the owner on 2026-11-05, continuing the exchange on constraint architectures), Response 1 §2, after Eppstein: "Computational complexity is not an intrinsic property of a configuration space by itself."
